name: ux2-u8-players
prompt:
Write public/js/players.js (new file, about 90 lines), a classic script loaded after main.js (STU-UX2: audio with a waveform). Wrap it in an IIFE. main.js renders each finished audio job as:
0:00
Cards are re-rendered often (innerHTML replaced), so work with event delegation and redraw new players. 1. Peaks cache: a Map from URL to a Promise of an array of numbers. peaks(url): fetch(url) -> arrayBuffer -> decode with a new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)() via decodeAudioData (the promise form) -> for 200 equal slices of channel 0 the largest absolute sample value -> close the context -> return the array. 2. draw(player): canvas = player.querySelector('canvas.wave'); set canvas.width = canvas.clientWidth * devicePixelRatio and canvas.height = canvas.clientHeight * devicePixelRatio (use 300 x 48 when clientWidth is 0); get peaks(player.dataset.src); scale them so the largest is 1; draw one bar per peak, centred vertically, bar height at least 1 px, with ctx.fillStyle = getComputedStyle(canvas).color; bars before the play position (audio.currentTime / audio.duration) use globalAlpha 1, the rest 0.45. Then set canvas.dataset.ready = '1'. On a failed fetch or decode leave it undrawn without throwing. 3. A MutationObserver on document.body (childList, subtree) and one pass on start: draw every .wave-player whose canvas has no data-ready yet. 4. Clicks (document listener): .wave-play -> play or pause that player's audio. Button state: on the audio's 'play' event set aria-label 'Pause' and add class playing to the player; on 'pause' and 'ended' set aria-label 'Play' and remove the class. Listen for these with document.addEventListener(type, handler, true) (media events do not bubble) and find the player with e.target.closest('.wave-player'). A click on canvas.wave seeks: audio.currentTime = (offsetX / canvas.clientWidth) * audio.duration; when the duration is not known yet (NaN), call audio.load() and seek on 'loadedmetadata' once. 5. 'timeupdate' (also captured on document): the player's .wave-time = m:ss of currentTime (seconds two digits) and redraw its bars from the cached peaks so the played part is brighter. Output only the file.
